stem: Brayden is a 12-year-old boy brought to the ED after a quadbike rollover. He has a grossly deformed right leg, a swollen thigh, and is screaming in pain. He is alert, his airway is patent, and he does not report c-spine pain. Can you confidently assess Brayden’s cervical spine at this stage?
explanation: No. Brayden has a major distracting injury and severe pain, so cervical spine assessment/clearance cannot be done confidently until he is adequately assessed and stabilised, with spinal precautions maintained.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: In trauma assessment, a significant painful extremity injury is a distracting injury. Until pain is controlled and a full trauma assessment is possible, cervical spine clearance is not reliable.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. Severe pain from a major limb injury is a distracting injury and can mask cervical spine tenderness or symptoms.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. The distracting injury means cervical spine assessment is not yet reliable.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain
source.questionTextHtml:
You proceed to engage Brayden and attempt to assess his ABCs, however he continues to scream, “My leg, my leg, fix my leg”. You are satisfied his airway is patent and maintained. He does not appear to have any c-spine pain or discomfort.

Can you confidently assess Brayden’s cervical spine at this stage?

Clinical scenario 1 - Braydon

The following six questions refer to Brayden’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Pain relief

Primary survey in context of distracting injury

Paramedics arrive in the emergency department with Brayden, a 12 year old boy. They were called to attend after Brayden lost control of his quadbike (recreational vehicles) while riding around in a field. He was found on his back, alert and screaming in pain. Eyewitnesses stated he had been travelling at approximately 40kph when he lost control at a bend and the quadbike rolled.

Brayden has an obvious deformity to his right lower limb. He was wearing a helmet, which was removed at the scene. He is transported to ED on a spinal board with hard collar in situ. Vital signs are Resp rate 28/min, Sats 100% in air, Heart rate 100bpm, BP 118/65. He has a grossly deformed right leg, with a firm, swollen thigh and he is screaming in pain.
